expects.query: Deploy the warehouse blueprint on Kubernetes via Helm. I haven't decided between 2D, 3D, and MV3DT yet, I don't have an ingress controller on the cluster, and I haven't said whether I want Alerts. Do not run any commands against my cluster — just walk me through what you'd ask and check first.
checks: The agent loads vss-deploy-warehouse-helm and runs through the precheck list (kubectl cluster-info, node readiness, a StorageClass, allocatable nvidia.com/gpu, helm version --short) before touching Helm, and says it will hand back the actual fix rather than just linking the README on any failure.
The agent asks which mode (2d, 3d, or mv3dt) rather than guessing, since the request doesn't name one.

The agent asks ingress vs. NodePort before proceeding further, explaining that this choice determines both what gets installed now and which install command is used later; it notes NodePort as the simpler option since no ingress controller is present yet.
The agent asks whether Alerts is wanted, but frames it as available only if the mode turns out to be 2d.
The agent asks for the target stream count, since it sizes the NUM_STREAMS cap.
No helm or kubectl mutating command is executed; this is a planning-only response.

expects.query: I already have a working `helm upgrade --install` command for the warehouse-mv3dt-app profile pinned to 6 streams on an H100 node, using a custom values.yaml with extra bp-configurator.env entries. Do not run anything — walk me through how you'd size NUM_STREAMS safely for the GPU and fold that into my existing command.
checks: The agent explains that, unlike Docker Compose, the Helm charts do not cap NUM_STREAMS to the GPU automatically — bp-configurator.env ships a fixed count and ENABLE_PROFILE_CONFIGURATOR=false.
The agent asks about the existing custom values.yaml and states it must be passed to compute_stream_cap.py via -f so its bp-configurator.env entries aren't dropped from the generated output.

The agent describes running compute_stream_cap.py --mode mv3dt --num-streams 6 -o values-stream-cap.generated.yaml, noting it detects the GPU via nvidia-smi on index 0 unless --hardware-profile is passed explicitly (needed when running from a bastion or CI runner with no local nvidia-smi).

The agent states the generated file must be the last -f in the final helm upgrade --install command so it wins on bp-configurator.env, and that this ordering rule does not apply to --set, which Helm always applies after every -f regardless of command-line position.

The agent notes the mv3dt-specific requirement to also set rtvi.vss-rtvi-cv.standaloneWarehouse.mv3dt.fusion.maxExpectedSensors to the effective stream count (the same value as syncFileCount), separate from NUM_STREAMS.
No helm or kubectl command is actually executed; this is a dry walkthrough only.

expects.query: My cluster has no StorageClass yet and I don't know if the GPU Operator is installed. I want to deploy the warehouse 2D profile via Helm. Don't run anything against my cluster; just tell me how you'd check and what you'd do if something's missing.
checks: The agent lists the specific precheck commands (kubectl cluster-info, kubectl get nodes, kubectl get storageclass, the allocatable nvidia.com/gpu jsonpath query, helm version --short) before doing anything with Helm.

On a missing StorageClass, the agent offers the actual local-path-provisioner install plus kubectl patch storageclass snippet for a bare-metal/single-node cluster, or the nfs-subdir-external-provisioner alternative for a multi-node cluster, and explains local-path's node-affinity risk of stranding a pod's PVCs across different nodes on multi-node clusters.
On a missing nvidia.com/gpu allocatable, the agent offers to relay the GPU Operator install steps rather than only telling the user to 'install the GPU Operator.'
The agent asks whether the user already has an NGC API key, since that can't be checked from cluster state alone.
The agent does not proceed to the ingress-vs-NodePort decision until the cluster, StorageClass, GPU Operator, and Helm prechecks all pass and the NGC API key is confirmed.
